decision.author: albanD
decision.body: Aren't you missing the frankenstein autograd functions in csrc/autograd/functions/* ?

inline_comments.body:
claude made a good comment that this is likely to trigger in the wild as it relies on us not doing something stupid manually but is not broadly tested in CI (as our CI runs without hooks enabled, so we never get to this code).
We could consider moving this check above the tls check?

Just for the record, explored moving this fire_node_creation_hooks into rebase_history/set_history.
While it would work for most things (modulo a refactor of saving variables before setting the history in codegen), inplace on view kill the dream as the output must be saved after the history rebase has happened. :(

@@ -0,0 +1,33 @@
+#pragma once
+
+#include <c10/core/SafePyObject.h>
+#include <c10/macros/Export.h>
+#include <vector>
+
+namespace at::impl {
+
+// TLS for torch.autograd.graph.node_creation_hook. Lives in ATen (rather than
+// torch/csrc/autograd) so that at::ThreadLocalState can snapshot it across
+// thread boundaries, e.g. into autograd engine worker threads. This mirrors
+// SavedTensorDefaultHooksTLS.
+struct TORCH_API NodeCreationHooksTLS {
+  // Hooks fire in registration order (outermost context manager first).
+  std::vector<c10::SafePyObject> stack;
+
+  // True while hooks are running; suppresses firing for nodes created by the
+  // hooks themselves to avoid unbounded recursion.
+  bool is_firing = false;

@@ -456,6 +457,78 @@ def disable_saved_tensors_hooks(error_message: str) -> Generator[None, None, Non
             torch._C._autograd._saved_tensors_hooks_disable(maybe_prev_message)
 
 
+class node_creation_hook:
+    """Context-manager that registers a hook called on each autograd Node created within it.
+
+    In that context, ``hook`` is called once for every autograd graph node
+    created by operations on tensors that require grad, with the freshly
+    created :class:`torch.autograd.graph.Node` as its only argument. The
+    intended use is to record the node, stash entries in ``node.metadata``,
+    or register backward hooks on it via
+    :meth:`~torch.autograd.graph.Node.register_hook` and
+    :meth:`~torch.autograd.graph.Node.register_prehook`.
+
+    The node is passed to the hook only once it is fully populated: its
+    ``next_functions`` are wired, all outputs' metadata are bound, and the
+    tensors saved for backward (``_saved_*``) have been stored, so a hook
+    that inspects the node sees its complete state.
+
+    The hook should have the following signature::
+
+        hook(node: torch.autograd.graph.Node) -> None
+
+    The registration is thread-local. It is captured into
+    :class:`~torch.autograd.graph.saved_tensors_hooks`-style thread-local
+    state, so it propagates to any worker thread that autograd (or another
+    subsystem built on it) spins up: if backward is run under this context
+    (or graph nodes are created during backward, e.g. with
+    ``create_graph=True`` or inside checkpoint recomputation), the hook also
+    fires for those nodes.

inline_comments.body: Isn't the standard practice to do innermost first?

inline_comments.body:
The argument is contrary to the behavior. If they are actually lazy, then they would get created in the context and thus be triggered.
We should just say that AccumulateGrad never triggers hooks.

+    outermost first.

+        >>> def creation_hook(node):

+        ...     # stand in for whatever thread-local state you want to restore
+        ...     # while this node runs in backward.
+        ...     region = current_region()
+        ...     node.register_prehook(lambda gO: enter_region(region))
+        ...     node.register_hook(lambda gI, gO: enter_region(None))

+        ...     loss = model(inputs)
